findings.problem: The explanation for "It's too wonderful for him to reach" quotes "Such knowledge is too wonderful for me, too lofty for me to attain," with a comma inside the quotation marks. Psalm 139:6 in the BSB ends "too lofty for me to attain." with a period.

rule.text: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included. A paraphrase uses no quotation marks.

findings.problem: The explanation for "He praises the LORD" quotes "I praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made," with a comma inside the quotation marks. The BSB (Psalm 139:14) has a period after "made" ("...wonderfully made. Marvelous are Your works...").

rule.text: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included. A paraphrase uses no quotation marks.

findings.problem: The explanation for "True" quotes "Search me, O God, and know my heart." with a period inside the quotation marks. The BSB (Psalm 139:23) has a semicolon there: "Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my concerns."

rule.text: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included. A paraphrase uses no quotation marks.

findings.problem: The explanation for "lead" quotes "See if there is any offensive way in me; lead me in the way everlasting," with a comma inside the quotation marks. Psalm 139:24 in the BSB ends with a period.

rule.text: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included. A paraphrase uses no quotation marks.

findings.problem: The explanation for "He praises the LORD" opens "Straight to praise! \"I praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made,\" David tells the LORD..." The quote speaks as "I," but David is only named after the quote.

rule.text: When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first.

findings.problem: The explanation for "lead" opens "Lead it is, and what a way to close out a psalm. \"See if there is any offensive way in me; lead me in the way everlasting,\" David prays..." The quote speaks in the first person ("in me," "lead me"), but David is only named after the quote.

rule.text: When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first.

findings.problem: The explanation for "leave" says "This whole psalm is about a God David can't get away from." That stretches the text. Psalm 139:7-12 is about not being able to get away from God's presence, but verses 19-22 are about the wicked and God's enemies, so the whole psalm isn't about that. The claim also carries no reference. Keep it to the verses, for example that earlier David asks where he could flee from God's presence (Psalm 139:7).

rule.text: **Don't stretch the text.** Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The explanation for "True" says of David's prayer in Psalm 139:23, "and he means it." That states David's inner sincerity as a fact. The text gives the prayer, not what was in David's heart as he said it. Mark it as Papa Dorin's own guess ("I bet he means it") or drop it.

rule.text: **Feelings.** He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The fix removed the capital-letter answer openers, but a formula is still there. Nearly every missed-answer explanation opens by echoing the answer back as a question: "Most, friend?" (1/4), "Writing it down?" (1/6), "Easy?" and "Long ago?" (1/8), "Let go?" (1/12), "Quiet?" (2/2), "Old friends?" (2/11), "Hide, friend?" (2/17). Right-answer explanations mostly open with a stock affirmation plus "friend": "You caught it, friend" (1/2), "Exactly, friend" (1/10), "You got it, friend" (1/12), "Right on, friend" (2/4), "That's it, friend" (2/8), "That's the one, friend" (2/11), "Yes, friend" (2/13). Nearly all 38 then follow "David says/tells the LORD in Psalm 139:N, '...'". Within single cards, the explanations also repeat each other: all three for 2/13 make the same point that David is being honest ("a raw, honest line, and he doesn't dress it up" / "honest with the LORD about exactly where he stands" / "isn't hiding anything in this prayer"), and both "lead" and "hide" on 2/17 land on "a Guide" ("Not a map, friend. A Guide." / "No hiding spot, just a Guide."). Both 2/8 explanations use the same build: "David tells God in Psalm 139:18, 'If I were to count them, they would outnumber the grains of sand' and/so..."

rule.text: There is no formula. Each explanation sounds natural and different from the others.
